title: The One It Didn't Hear
story_question: Can Alaska hear a mountain before it falls?

lines.text: Alaska buried seismometers to hear earthquakes.
Researchers taught two hundred of those sensors a second job. Hearing landslides.
A quake ends in seconds. A slide rumbles for a minute. A program watches for that.
It searches only one stretch of coast.
Last August a mountain fell into Tracy Arm, south of Juneau.
It fell outside the search area, so no alarm fired.
The sensors still heard it. A scientist found the slide by hand.
And a harder limit remains. Rock makes no sound until it falls.
So a federal grant sent one point seven seven million dollars to the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
To build a simulated mountain, fed by those sensors, that forecasts what a slope will do.
The work starts next month and takes years.
The sensors keep listening, but never ahead.

gate_0e_v1_failures_fixed: 'the coverage' arrived with a definite article, never established. FIXED by L3, which establishes that two hundred cannot cover Alaska and that they watch one stretch of coast, BEFORE L5 refers back to 'that stretch'.
'the algorithm' arrived with a definite article, never established. FIXED by removing it entirely. L6 now says a scientist found the slide by hand.

'Nothing heard it' contradicted 'ran the algorithm by hand'. FIXED and made MORE accurate to the source. The sensors did record the ground motion; what did not happen was an automatic detection. L5 and L6 now say exactly that.
'a working copy of a mountain' was undefined. FIXED by L9, a simulated mountain, fed live data, that models what comes next.
'Until then' pointed at August when nothing finishes in August. FIXED by L10, which says the work takes years, and by dropping 'until then' from the button.
'them' could attach to earthquakes. FIXED by naming 'sensors' explicitly in L1.
'A slide sounds different' was different from an unstated thing. FIXED by L2, which states both durations side by side.

A search boundary and a hearing boundary are different things, and that is exactly what the source says (no automatic detection, data existed, algorithm applied manually).
'the alarm' appeared only in the negative and was never introduced. FIXED, an automatic search is established one line before the alarm fails to fire.
